result.note: Tests the July 2026 customs duty exemptions on electronics components and battery machinery, and India's electronics manufacturing target; Apple-specific details skipped.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, the Union government exempted certain electronics components and battery-making machinery from import duties. Consider the following statements about these exemptions:
items: The exemptions are valid until March 31, 2029.
The exemptions cover 85 types of assembly machinery, aimed at anchoring the electric mobility and battery ecosystem domestically.
The tariffs removed on parts for wireless charging and automotive displays ranged from 10% to 15%.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the exemptions wipe out tariffs of 5% to 7.5% on parts for wireless charging, lithium-ion cell production equipment and automotive displays. By cutting duties on inputs while keeping them on finished goods, India aims to push manufacturers beyond simple assembly.
questions.source: The rules wipe out 5% to 7.5% tariffs on parts for wireless charging, lithium-ion cell production equipment, and automotive displays.

questions.prompt: As of July 2026, what is India's target for the scale of electronics manufacturing by fiscal year 2030?
questions.explain: The government aims to scale electronics manufacturing to USD 500 billion by fiscal year 2030, and the July 2026 duty exemptions feed into that goal. Smartphone manufacturing has risen 28-fold over the last decade.
questions.source: The tax holiday feeds into New Delhi’s aggressive target to scale electronics manufacturing to USD 500 billion by fiscal year 2030, of which smartphone manufacturing has risen 28-fold over the last decade.
